title: Audit stale Option B proposal, WBS, delivery estimate, and 18888 payment-draft lineage without authorizing a project, Worker, payment, or chain effect
reason: PR 182 contains useful fail-closed candidate fields and tests, but it accepts caller-shaped Customer references, cost and schedule inputs; describes an unverified direction with binding and accepted terminology; creates role-scoped WBS branches under codex/*; carries stale closed dependency identifiers; and embeds an open unmerged PR 186 payment-draft lineage with fixed Mainnet addresses and caller-injected read adapters. Current main has a newer side-effect-free engineering-cycle planner and later company-runtime safety work. The safe action is a current-main audit record only, with no proposal, payment, Worker, branch plan, wallet, workflow, revenue, signer, or chain capability transplanted.

inventory.security_blocker: No immutable Customer acceptance, financial authority, funded approved budget, canonical beneficiary, deployed escrow, authoritative Worker/reviewer registry, main-tracked ABI/runtime-codehash binding, or authorized payment adapter exists for PR 182.

blocking_findings: PR 182 is open, Draft, unmerged, diverged, and 743 commits behind exact current main.
createOperatingCompanyBindingProposal requires only a caller-supplied conditional_acceptance_reference and cannot resolve it to an immutable Human decision artifact.

The API and fields use BindingProposal and accepted_direction_at terminology even though conditional_acceptance_verified, engineering_preparation_authorized, project_activated, payment_requested, and payment_received are always false; publishing these names without the fail-closed context could misstate acceptance or authority.

The 108888 KAIOS cost model, five milestone amounts, Customer label, delivery dates, roles, capacity, payment policies, dependencies, scopes, hours, and acceptance-test labels are caller or fixture data, not Canon or Human-authorized commercial facts.

createOptionBWorkBreakdown explicitly requires codex/* branches, while the current integration boundary forbids merging through that wake-triggering path and current main's newer planner rejects codex/* branches.

WBS packages reject assigned_worker_id but still accept caller-shaped role, trust requirement, file scope, dependency, hours, branch, start gate, and acceptance-test labels without resolving an authoritative Worker, Reviewer, Claim, lease, or fencing token.

estimateOptionBDeliverySchedule derives dates from caller-supplied hours and capacity; it does not prove staff availability, accepted scope, Human gates, reviewer capacity, or a binding delivery commitment.

The embedded PR 186 payment draft fixes BSC Mainnet contract and beneficiary addresses in code even though address publication does not prove controller, signer, beneficiary, budget, treasury, or payment authority.

readKaios18888PaymentReadiness accepts a caller-injected bankReader and caller-supplied proposer and approver addresses; this can model read shapes but cannot authenticate deployed ABI, proxy implementation, runtime codehash, roles, beneficiary, or authorization.

The payment request's budget_id, requested_by, purpose, nonce, amount, and timing are caller inputs; the resulting NON_AUTHORITATIVE_PAYMENT_DRAFT is not a payment request, approval, funded obligation, receivable, escrow, or revenue event.
PR 186 remains open Draft and unmerged, so PR 182 cannot treat its payment-draft code as an accepted dependency or current-main capability.
The fixture dependency list PR169, PR170, and PR176 is stale: all three are now closed unmerged and cannot authorize Option B work.

Current main has no Option B or KAIOS_18888_PAYMENT_CONFIG symbols and contains later company-runtime and universal-test changes; overwriting it with the stale files would discard subsequent safety work.

Historical exact-head CI proves only internal behavior of the old candidate. It cannot manufacture Customer acceptance, Company authority, Worker/reviewer eligibility, budget, custody, beneficiary, signer, deployment, payment, revenue, delivery, or chain facts.

The WBS rejects assigned_worker_id and returns null Worker, Claim, and fencing-token fields with DRAFT_WBS_NOT_DISPATCHABLE.
The schedule is explicitly non-binding and blocks completion when reviewer capacity is zero.
The embedded payment draft returns calls=null and calldata=null, requests no signer, sends no transaction, and keeps authority, budget, beneficiary, ABI, and runtime-codehash gates false.

Keep all payment artifacts non-executable until a separate explicitly authorized path exists; never emit calldata, request a signer, broadcast, recognize revenue, mutate treasury, or claim a receipt from this lineage audit.

Never access credentials, request wallet approval, transfer assets, appoint a signer/controller/operator, dispatch workflows, call paid APIs, launch an external agent, activate Workers/Life, send a Mainnet transaction, or mutate chain state as part of this audit.
